                                                                                                                       LTC4368
                                                                                                    100V UV/OV and Reverse
                                                                                                    Protection Controller with
                                                                                                  Bidirectional Circuit Breaker
Features                                                                                           Description
nn Wide Operating Voltage Range: 2.5V to 60V                                                           The LTC®4368 protects applications from power supply
nn Overvoltage Protection to 100V                                                                      voltages that may be too high, too low, or even negative
nn Reverse Supply Protection to –40V                                                                   and from overcurrent faults in both forward and reverse
nn Bidirectional Electronic Circuit Breaker:                                                           directions. The LTC4368 controls the gate voltage of a pair
   nn +50mV Forward Sense Threshold                                                                    of external N-channel MOSFETs to ensure that the load
   nn –50mV Reverse (LTC4368-1)                                                                        is connected to the input supply only when there are no
   nn –3mV Reverse (LTC4368-2)                                                                         voltage or current faults.
nn Adjustable ±1.5% Undervoltage and Overvoltage
                                                                                                       Two comparator inputs allow configuration of the over-
   Thresholds                                                                                          voltage (OV) and undervoltage (UV) set points using an
nn Low Operating Current: 80µA
                                                                                                       external resistive divider. A current sense resistor sets the
nn Low Shutdown Current: 5µA
                                                                                                       forward and reverse circuit breaker current thresholds.
nn Controls Back-to-Back N-Channel MOSFETs
                                                                                                       After a forward current fault, the LTC4368 will either latch
nn Blocks 50Hz and 60Hz AC Power
                                                                                                       off power, or retry after a user adjustable delay. After a
nn Hot Swappable Supply Input
                                                                                                       reverse current fault, the LTC4368 waits for the output to
nn Pin-Selectable Overcurrent Auto-Retry Timer or Latchoff
                                                                                                       fall 100mV below the input to reconnect power to the load.
nn 10-Pin MSOP and 3mm × 3mm DFN Packages
                                                                                                       The LTC4368 has a 32ms turn-on delay that debounces
Applications                                                                                           live supply input connections and blocks 50Hz and 60Hz
                                                                                                       AC power. UV/OV faults also trigger the 32ms recovery
nn Reverse Battery Protection                                                                          delay before the external MOSFETs are turned back on.
nn Portable Instrumentation                                                                            L, LT, LTC, LTM, Linear Technology and the Linear logo are registered trademarks and
nn Automotive and Industrial Surge Protection                                                          ThinSOT is a trademark of Linear Technology Corporation. All other trademarks are the property
                                                                                                       of their respective owners.
nn Energy Storage Systems

Pin Functions
Exposed Pad: The exposed pad may be left open or con-                  disconnecting the load from the input. After a reverse
nected to device ground.                                               current fault, when VOUT falls 100mV below VIN, the
                                                                       LTC4368 automatically turns on the external MOSFETs.
FAULT: Fault Indication Output. Connect to a pull-up resis-
                                                                       A forward overcurrent fault uses the RETRY pin to set the
tor. This high voltage open drain output is pulled low if there
is a voltage or current fault, if SHDN is low, or if VIN has           conditions for reconnecting power to the load. Connect
not risen above VIN(UVLO). Leave unconnected if unused.                to VOUT if unused.
                                                                       SHDN: Shutdown Control Input. Assuming no voltage or
GATE: Gate Drive Output for External N-channel MOSFETs.
                                                                       current faults, SHDN high enables the GATE charge pump
An internal charge pump provides 35µA of pull-up current
                                                                       which in turn enhances the gate of the external N-channel
and up to 13.1V of enhancement to the gate of an external
                                                                       MOSFETs. A low on SHDN generates a pull down on the
MOSFET. When turned off, GATE is pulled just below the
                                                                       GATE output with a 90µA current sink and places the
lower of VIN or VOUT. When VIN goes negative, GATE is
automatically connected to VIN.                                        LTC4368 in low current mode (5µA). If a forward overcur-
                                                                       rent condition latches off the external MOSFETs (RETRY
GND: Device Ground.                                                    grounded), the SHDN pin must be toggled low then high
OV: Overvoltage Comparator Input. Connect this pin to an               to re-enable the charge pump that enhances the external
external resistive divider to set the desired VIN overvolt-            MOSFETs. If VIN goes above 80V, the SHDN pin voltage
age fault threshold. This input connects an accurate, fast             must be kept below 80V.
(1µs) comparator with a 0.5V rising threshold and 25mV                 UV: Undervoltage Comparator Input. Connect this pin to an
of hysteresis. When OV rises above its threshold, a 60mA               external resistive divider to set the desired VIN undervoltage
current sink pulls down on the GATE output. When OV                    fault threshold. This input connects to an accurate, fast
falls back below 0.475V, and after a 32ms GATE turn-on                 (1µs) comparator with a 0.5V falling threshold and 25mV
delay waiting period, the GATE charge pump is enabled.                 of hysteresis. When UV falls below its threshold, a 60mA
The low leakage current on this input allows the use of                current sink pulls down on the GATE output. When UV
large valued resistors for the external resistive divider.             rises back above 0.525V, and after a 32ms GATE turn-on
Connect to GND if unused.                                              delay waiting period, the GATE charge pump is enabled.
RETRY: Retry or Latch-Off Selection Input. Connect to                  The low leakage current on this input allows the use of
ground to latch off the MOSFETs after a forward overcurrent            large valued resistors for the external resistive divider. If
fault. To turn the external MOSFETs back on, the SHDN                  unused and VIN is less than 80V, connect to VIN with a
pin must be toggled low then high. Connect RETRY to an                 510k resistor.
external capacitor to configure a 5.5ms/nF delay before                VIN: Power Supply Input. Maximum protection range: –40V
the MOSFETs automatically turn on again. Leave uncon-                  to 100V. Operating range: 2.5V to 60V. This pin can be
nected if unused.                                                      hot swapped and has a 2.2V UVLO.
SENSE: Overcurrent Sense Input. Connect a current                      VOUT: Output Voltage Sense Input. Connect a current sense
sense resistor between SENSE and VOUT. This input                      resistor between VOUT and SENSE. The GATE charge pump

Operation
Many of today’s electronic systems get their power from                of a single catastrophic event, or over time as devices
external sources such as wall adapters, batteries and                  degrade from repeated overstress.
custom power supplies. Figure 1 shows a supply arrange-                The LTC4368 limits these errant overvoltage and overcur-
ment using a DC barrel connector. Power is supplied by                 rent conditions and helps extend the life of the electronic
an AC adapter or, if the plug is withdrawn, by a removable             systems it protects. When the part detects an overcurrent
battery. Note that the polarity of the AC adapter and barrel           or overvoltage fault, it isolates the input supply from the
connector varies by manufacturer. Trouble arises when                  load by turning off the external back-to-back MOSFETs.
any of the following occurs:
                                                                       The LTC4368 provides accurate overvoltage and under-
• The battery is installed backwards                                   voltage comparators to ensure that power is applied to
• A wall adapter of opposite polarity is attached                      the load only if the input supply meets the user selectable
                                                                       voltage window. Additionally, two accurate overcurrent
• A wall adapter of excessive voltage is attached
                                                                       comparators disconnect the load from the supply when
• A wall adapter with an AC output is attached                         excessive current flows in either the forward (+50mV/
• The battery is discharged below a safe level                         RSENSE) or reverse (–50mV or –3mV/RSENSE) direction.
                                                                       Reverse supply voltage protection circuits automatically
• The load or the input is shorted to ground or to another             isolate the load from negative input voltages. During normal
  supply                                                               operation, a high voltage charge pump enhances the gate
• Excessive current flows from the supply to the load or               of dual external N-channel power MOSFETs, thus providing
  from the load to the supply                                          a low loss path for qualified power. Power consumption
                                                                       is 5µA during shutdown and 80µA while operating. The
These conditions, if unchecked, can damage electronic                  LTC4368 integrates all these functions in small 10-lead
systems and their connectors. Damage can take the form                 3mm × 3mm DFN and MSOP packages.

As shown in Figure 11, external back-to-back N-channel
MOSFETs are required for reverse supply protection. When
VIN goes negative, the reverse VIN comparator closes the                                                                 VOUT

internal switch, which in turn connects the gates of the
external MOSFETs to the negative VIN voltage. The body                                        5V/DIV
                                                                                                                                GATE
diode (D1) of M1 turns on, but the body diode (D2) of M2                                       –20V
remains in reverse blocking mode. This means that the                                                                   VIN
common source connection of M1 and M2 remains about
a diode drop higher than VIN. Since the gate voltage of                                                                            LTC4368 F12

M2 is shorted to VIN, M2 will be turned off and no current
can flow from VOUT to VIN. Note that the voltage rating of                                             Figure 12. Hot Swapping VIN to –20V

                                                                                         The SHDN input turns off the external MOSFETs in a slow,
                                                                                         controlled manner. When SHDN is asserted low, a 90µA
          10V/DIV                                                                        current sink slowly begins to turn off the external MOSFETs.
                                  GREEN (TOP): MOSFET GATE                               Once the voltage at the GATE pin falls below the voltage
                                BLUE (BOTTOM): MOSFET SOURCE                             at the VOUT pin, the current sink is throttled back and a
                                                                                         feedback loop takes over. This loop forces the GATE voltage
                                                                                         to track VOUT, thus keeping the external MOSFETs off as
                                                           4368 F13
                                      100ns/DIV

                                                                                         VOUT decays. Note that when VOUT < 2.5V, the GATE pin
                Figure 13. Hot Swapping VIN to +48V
                                                                                         is pulled all the way to ground.

illustrated in Figures 5 and 6. Going out of and then back                                      5V/DIV

into fault in fewer than 32ms will keep the MOSFET off                                                   SHDN

continuously. Similarly, coming out of shutdown (SHDN                                             GND

Transients During OV Fault                                                                      Layout Considerations
The circuit of Figure 19 is used to illustrate transients                                       The trace length between the VIN pin and the drain of the
commonly encountered during an overvoltage condition.                                           external MOSFET should be minimized, as well as the
The nominal input supply is 48V and it has an overvoltage                                       trace length between the GATE pin of the LTC4368 and
threshold of 60V. The parasitic inductance is that of a 1                                       the gates of the external MOSFETs. The SENSE and VOUT
foot wire (roughly 300nH). Figure 20 shows the waveforms                                        pins must be connected with traces that tie directly and
during on overvoltage condition at VIN. These transients                                        solely to the sense resistor.
depend on the parasitic inductance and resistance of the                                        Place the bypass capacitors at VOUT as close as possible
wire along with the capacitance at the VIN node. D1 is an
                                                                                                to the external MOSFET. Use high frequency ceramic
optional power clamp (TVS, TransZorb) recommended for                                           capacitors in addition to bulk capacitors to mitigate hot
applications where the DC input voltage can exceed 24V                                          swap ringing. Place the high frequency capacitors closest
and with large VIN parasitic inductance. No clamp was                                           to the MOSFET. Note that bulk capacitors mitigate ringing
used to capture the waveforms of Figure 20. In order to                                         by virtue of their ESR. Ceramic capacitors have low ESR
maintain reverse supply protection, D1 must be a bidirec-                                       and can thus ring near their resonant frequency. The trace
tional clamp with appropriate voltage and power ratings.                                        length of the GATE pin should be kept as small as possible,
                                                                                                and the number of components connected to the GATE
                                                                                                pin should also be minimized.
                                                                                                The SOA of the external MOSFET might require the board to
                                                                                                have a minimum total area as well as a minimum amount
                                                                                                of trace volume connected to the drain and source pins.
